## database package

Laravel-style migrations and seeders that run unchanged on Postgres, MySQL and sqlite.

## Remarks

Migrations describe tables in dialect-neutral terms through [Schema](./database.schema.md) and [Blueprint](./database.blueprint.md)<!-- -->; a [Grammar](./database.grammar.md) compiles them to SQL for whichever database is configured. Switching database means changing one environment variable, not rewriting migrations.

The layers, from the bottom up:

- [createConnection()](./database.createconnection.md) / [Connection](./database.connection.md) — a driver-agnostic handle, configured by [configFromEnv()](./database.configfromenv.md)<!-- -->. Drivers are optional peer dependencies loaded lazily. - [Grammar](./database.grammar.md) — compiles blueprints to a dialect's SQL. - [Schema](./database.schema.md) / [Blueprint](./database.blueprint.md) / [ColumnDefinition](./database.columndefinition.md) — the builder a migration writes against. - [Migration](./database.migration.md) / [Migrator](./database.migrator.md) — discovery, ordering, batching and rollback. - [Seeder](./database.seeder.md) / [SeederRunner](./database.seederrunner.md) — portable seed data. - [runConsole()](./database.runconsole.md) — the CLI an application wires up.

\#\#\# Release tags

Everything here carries a TSDoc release tag:

- `@public` — the supported surface: migrations, seeders, the schema builder, connections and configuration. - `@beta` — usable, but still moving. Two groups: the grammar extension point ([Grammar](./database.grammar.md) and friends, [ColumnAttributes](./database.columnattributes.md)<!-- -->, [IndexDefinition](./database.indexdefinition.md)<!-- -->, [ForeignKeyDefinition](./database.foreignkeydefinition.md)<!-- -->), whose protected surface will grow as the builder learns more modifiers; and the `ALTER TABLE` path ([Blueprint.dropColumn()](./database.blueprint.dropcolumn.md)<!-- -->, [Blueprint.dropIndex()](./database.blueprint.dropindex.md)<!-- -->, [Schema.rename()](./database.schema.rename.md)<!-- -->), which is thin and the least exercised across the three dialects. - `@internal` — not exported from this entry point, and free to change. - `@alpha` — deliberately unused. API Extractor drops `@alpha` class methods from the doc model outright, so on a method it behaves like `@internal` rather than like a weaker `@beta`<!-- -->.
